newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila futures bourse tightens membership rules.
newsitem.headline: Manila futures bourse tightens membership rules.

text.p: The Philippine Futures Exchange has set up stricter membership criteria to prevent member-brokers from reneging on obligations and leaving their clients with open contracts.

In a position paper submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission, acting president Simeon Valdez said the board had decided to put all membership fees into an escrow account as guarantees against claims.

"The by-laws provision was amended to provide for a feature that the membership and the seat of the corporate trading members should be surrendered to and held in escrow by the exchange as guarantee and collateral for any possible claims of clients," he said.
The member will lose his membership once his contribution is withdrawn from the fund for whatever reason, Valdez added.
The exchange also cut the number of members to 50 from 76.
The exchange is in the process of instituting reforms after it was closed down by the SEC last June following reports of widespread irregularities.
Last February, the exchange asked for a two-month extension as the SEC threatened to revoke its licence.
Before its closure, the exchange had less than 10 active brokers.
The bourse traded in copra, sugar, dry cocoon, soybean, coffee and major currencies.
